title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 22. The Festival of the Meeting of Sri Nityananda and Advaita
html:
Nityananda comes to Gauda: His bathing and adornment in the house of Raghava Pandita at Panihati; play with His cowherd friends; Gadadhara Dasa; Saptagrama and the Triveni; Uddharana; the meeting with Advaita at Shantipura

Verse 1

ततश्च श्रीगौरचन्द्रो भक्तवर्गसमन्वितः।
नित्यानन्दं पुनरपि प्राह प्रहसिताननः॥१॥

tataśca śrīgauracandro bhaktavargasamanvitaḥ|
nityānandaṁ punarapi prāha prahasitānanaḥ||1||

tatah cha — and then; shri-gaurachandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; bhakta-varga-samanvitah — surrounded by the host of devotees; nityanandam — to Nityananda; punah api — again; praha — said; prahasita-ananah — with a smiling face.

1Then Sri Gaurachandra, surrounded by the host of His devotees, smiled and spoke to Nityananda again:

Verse 2

पूर्वं यत् कथितं तच्च कर्तव्यं भवता किल।
गच्छ गौडं हि तच्छ्रुत्वा स जगाम हसन् प्रभुः॥२॥

pūrvaṁ yat kathitaṁ tacca kartavyaṁ bhavatā kila|
gaccha gauḍaṁ hi tacchrutvā sa jagāma hasan prabhuḥ||2||

purvam — before; yat — what; kathitam — was said; tat — that; cha — and; kartavyam — is to be done; bhavata — by You; kila — surely; gachchha — go; gaudam — to Gauda; hi — then; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; sah — He; jagama — went; hasan — laughing; prabhuh — the Prabhu.

2"What I told You before You must surely carry out: go now to Gauda!" Hearing this, the Prabhu set off laughing

Verse 3

पानिहाटं पुरं रम्यं राघवपण्डितालयम्।
प्रणमन्तं द्विजं क्रोडीकृत्वा प्राह महासुखी॥३॥

pānihāṭaṁ puraṁ ramyaṁ rāghavapaṇḍitālayam|
praṇamantaṁ dvijaṁ kroḍīkṛtvā prāha mahāsukhī||3||

panihatam — to Panihati; puram — the town; ramyam — lovely; raghava-pandita-alayam — the home of Raghava Pandita; pranamantam — who was bowing; dvijam — the brahmana; krodikritva — clasping to His breast; praha — said; maha-sukhi — in great joy.

3to the lovely town of Panihati1, where Raghava Pandita had his home. The brahmana bowed before Him, and He, in great joy, clasped him to His breast and said:

Verse 4

राघव कुरु शीघ्रं मे सुवासितजलैरपि।
अभिषेकं चन्दनादिपुष्पालङ्करणादिना॥४॥

rāghava kuru śīghraṁ me suvāsitajalairapi|
abhiṣekaṁ candanādipuṣpālaṅkaraṇādinā||4||

raghava — O Raghava; kuru — perform; shighram — quickly; me — My; suvasita-jalaih — with fragrant water; api — and; abhishekam — ceremonial bath; chandana-adi-pushpa-alankarana-adina — with sandal, flowers, ornaments and the rest.

4"Raghava, quickly perform My ceremonial bath with fragrant water, and adorn Me with sandal, flowers and all the rest.

Verse 5

स्वर्णरौप्यप्रवालादिमणिमुक्तादिनिर्मितैः।
भूषणैश्च त्वया कार्यं मदङ्गपरिमण्डनम्॥५॥

svarṇaraupyapravālādimaṇimuktādinirmitaiḥ|
bhūṣaṇaiśca tvayā kāryaṁ madaṅgaparimaṇḍanam||5||

svarna-raupya-pravala-adi-mani-mukta-adi-nirmitaih — made of gold, silver, coral, gems, pearls and the like; bhushanaih — with ornaments; cha — and; tvaya — by you; karyam — is to be done; mat-anga-parimandanam — the adorning of My body.

5Adorn My body with jewels as well — of gold, silver, coral, gems and pearls —

Verse 6

येन मे प्राणनाथस्य गौरचन्द्रस्य सर्वदा।
सच्चिदानन्दपूर्णस्य पूर्णो मनोरथो भवेत्॥६॥

yena me prāṇanāthasya gauracandrasya sarvadā|
saccidānandapūrṇasya pūrṇo manoratho bhavet||6||

yena — so that by this; me — My; prana-nathasya — of the Lord of life; gaurachandrasya — of Gaurachandra; sarvada — ever; sat-chit-ananda-purnasya — full of eternity, knowledge and bliss; purnah — fulfilled; mano-rathah — the heart's desire; bhavet — may be.

6so that the heart's desire of Gaurachandra, the Lord of My life, ever full of being, consciousness and bliss, may be fulfilled."

Verse 7

श्रुत्वा सर्वं शीघ्रमेव कारयित्वा जनैर्द्विजः।
सुगन्धिपयसा सुरदीर्घिकाया मुदान्वितः॥७॥

śrutvā sarvaṁ śīghrameva kārayitvā janairdvijaḥ|
sugandhipayasā suradīrghikāyā mudānvitaḥ||7||

shrutva — hearing; sarvam — everything; shighram eva — at once; karayitva — having it prepared; janaih — by people; dvijah — the brahmana; sugandhi-payasa — with fragrant water; sura-dirghikayah — of the river of the gods (the Ganga); muda anvitah — full of joy.

7Hearing all this, the brahmana joyfully had everything prepared at once by his people; with the fragrant water of the river of the gods2

Verse 8

स्नापयित्वा संनिमज्य भूषयित्वा स भूषणैः।
गन्धचन्दनपुष्पैश्च ननाम भुवि दण्डवत्॥८॥

snāpayitvā saṁnimajya bhūṣayitvā sa bhūṣaṇaiḥ|
gandhacandanapuṣpaiśca nanāma bhuvi daṇḍavat||8||

snapayitva — having bathed (Him); samnimajya — immersing; bhushayitva — having adorned; sah — he; bhushanaih — with ornaments; gandha-chandana-pushpaih — with scents, sandal and flowers; cha — and; nanama — bowed; bhuvi — on the ground; danda-vat — like a rod.

8he bathed Him, immersing Him in it, adorned Him with jewels, with scents, sandal and flowers, and fell before Him on the ground like a rod.

Verse 9

सर्वालङ्कारसंयुक्तो रेजे नन्दसुतो यथा।
बलदेवः स्वयं चापि स्वयं गोपालरूपधृक्॥९॥

sarvālaṅkārasaṁyukto reje nandasuto yathā|
baladevaḥ svayaṁ cāpi svayaṁ gopālarūpadhṛk||9||

sarva-alankara-samyuktah — adorned with every ornament; reje — shone; nanda-sutah — the son of Nanda; yatha — like; baladevah — Baladeva; svayam — Himself; cha api — and indeed; svayam — Himself; gopala-rupa-dhrik — bearing the form of a cowherd boy.

9Adorned with every ornament, He shone like the son of Nanda — for He is Baladeva Himself, who Himself has taken the form of a cowherd boy.

Verse 10

श्रीदामाद्याः सखा ये च व्रजगोपालरूपिणः।
वंशीवेणुविषाणाद्यैरलङ्कारैश्च मण्डिताः॥१०॥

śrīdāmādyāḥ sakhā ye ca vrajagopālarūpiṇaḥ|
vaṁśīveṇuviṣāṇādyairalaṅkāraiśca maṇḍitāḥ||10||

shridama-adyah — headed by Shridama; sakhah — the friends; ye — who; cha — and; vraja-gopala-rupinah — in the form of the cowherd boys of Vraja; vamshi-venu-vishana-adyaih — with vamshi and venu flutes, horns and the like; alankaraih — with ornaments; cha — and; manditah — adorned.

10And His friends headed by Shridama, in the form of the cowherd boys of Vraja, adorned with vamshi and venu flutes, horns and other ornaments —

Verse 11

श्रीरामसुन्दरगौरीदासाद्याः कीर्तनप्रियाः।
विहरन्ति सदा नित्यानन्दसङ्गे महत्तमाः॥११॥

śrīrāmasundaragaurīdāsādyāḥ kīrtanapriyāḥ|
viharanti sadā nityānandasaṅge mahattamāḥ||11||

shri-rama-sundara-gauridasa-adyah — Sri Rama, Sundara, Gauridasa and others; kirtana-priyah — lovers of kirtana; viharanti — sport; sada — always; nityananda-sange — in the company of Nityananda; mahattamah — the greatest of souls.

11Sri Rama, Sundara, Gauridasa3 and other great souls who love kirtana — ever sport in Nityananda's company.

Verse 12

एवं स भगवान् रामस्तैः सार्धं जाह्नवीजले।
क्रीडन् ताण्डवमासाद्य स्वभक्तानां गृहे गृहे॥१२॥

evaṁ sa bhagavān rāmastaiḥ sārdhaṁ jāhnavījale|
krīḍan tāṇḍavamāsādya svabhaktānāṁ gṛhe gṛhe||12||

evam — thus; sah — He; bhagavan — the Lord; ramah — Rama; taih sardham — together with them; jahnavi-jale — in the waters of the Jahnavi (Ganga); kridan — sporting; tandavam — the tandava dance; asadya — taking up; sva-bhaktanam — of His devotees; grihe grihe — in house after house.

12Thus the Lord Rama played with them in the waters of the Jahnavi and danced the tandava in house after house of His devotees;

Verse 13

रममाणः सुखेनापि गदाधरगृहं ययौ।
गोपीभावेन पूर्णः स दृष्ट्वा तं प्रेमविह्वलः॥१३॥

ramamāṇaḥ sukhenāpi gadādharagṛhaṁ yayau|
gopībhāvena pūrṇaḥ sa dṛṣṭvā taṁ premavihvalaḥ||13||

ramamanah — rejoicing; sukhena — blissfully; api — and; gadadhara-griham — to the house of Gadadhara; yayau — came; gopi-bhavena — with the mood of the gopis; purnah — filled; sah — he (Gadadhara); drishtva — seeing; tam — Him; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed with love.

13rejoicing in bliss, He came to the house of Gadadhara4. Gadadhara, filled with the mood of the gopis, was overwhelmed with love on seeing Him;

Verse 14

आगतः कीर्तनानन्दः सप्तग्रामाख्यकं पुरम्।
त्रिवेणीतीरमासाद्य गौराङ्गगुणकीर्तने॥१४॥

āgataḥ kīrtanānandaḥ saptagrāmākhyakaṁ puram|
triveṇītīramāsādya gaurāṅgaguṇakīrtane||14||

agatah — having come; kirtana-anandah — blissful in kirtana; sapta-grama-akhyakam — called Saptagrama; puram — to the town; triveni-tiram — the bank of the Triveni; asadya — reaching; gauranga-guna-kirtane — in the singing of Gauranga's qualities.

14together with Him, blissful in kirtana, he came to the town of Saptagrama5, and on the bank of the Triveni, while Gauranga's qualities were being sung,

Verse 15

ननर्त परमानन्दं गोपीभावं प्रदर्शयन्।
नित्यानन्दोऽपि गौराङ्गकीर्तनानन्ददायकः॥१५॥

nanarta paramānandaṁ gopībhāvaṁ pradarśayan|
nityānando'pi gaurāṅgakīrtanānandadāyakaḥ||15||

nanarta — danced; parama-anandam — supreme bliss; gopi-bhavam — the mood of the gopis; pradarshayan — displaying; nityanandah — Nityananda; api — and; gauranga-kirtana-ananda-dayakah — the giver of the bliss of Gauranga's kirtana.

15he danced in supreme bliss, displaying the mood of the gopis. And Nityananda, the giver of the bliss of Gauranga's kirtana,

Verse 16

कृत्वा तस्मिन्महोल्लासं पुरन्दरगृहं ययौ।
तस्य प्रेमरसेनापि कृत्वा तस्य सुखं च सः॥१६॥

kṛtvā tasminmahollāsaṁ purandaragṛhaṁ yayau|
tasya premarasenāpi kṛtvā tasya sukhaṁ ca saḥ||16||

kritva — making; tasmin — there; maha-ullasam — great rejoicing; purandara-griham — to the house of Purandara; yayau — went; tasya — his; prema-rasena — with the rasa of love; api — and; kritva — giving; tasya — to him; sukham — happiness; cha — and; sah — He.

16having raised great rejoicing there, went to the house of Purandara6 and gave him happiness with the rasa of love.

Verse 17

यत्र सप्तर्षयः सर्वे स्मरन्ति भावतः पदम्।
मुक्तवेणीतयाख्यातं वदन्ति वेदपारगाः॥१७॥

yatra saptarṣayaḥ sarve smaranti bhāvataḥ padam|
muktaveṇītayākhyātaṁ vadanti vedapāragāḥ||17||

yatra — where; sapta-rishayah — the seven sages; sarve — all; smaranti — remember; bhavatah — with love; padam — the feet (of the Lord); mukta-veni-taya — as Mukta-veni; akhyatam — named; vadanti — declare; veda-paragah — those versed in the Vedas.

17There, where all the seven sages lovingly remember the feet of the Lord — the place that the knowers of the Vedas call Mukta-veni7 —

Verse 18

गङ्गायमुनयोश्चैव सरस्वत्याश्च सर्वदा।
प्रवाहाश्च वहन्ति स्म तद्दर्शनमहोत्सवाः॥१८॥

gaṅgāyamunayoścaiva sarasvatyāśca sarvadā|
pravāhāśca vahanti sma taddarśanamahotsavāḥ||18||

ganga-yamunayoh — of the Ganga and the Yamuna; cha eva — and; sarasvatyah — of the Sarasvati; cha — and; sarvada — ever; pravahah — the currents; cha — and; vahanti sma — flow; tat-darshana-maha-utsavah — the sight of which is a great festival.

18the currents of the Ganga, the Yamuna and the Sarasvati ever flow, and to see them is a great festival.

Verse 19

नरा मुक्ता भवन्ति हि स्नात्वा वा स्मरणादपि।
हरौ भक्तिं च विन्दन्ति सर्वदुःखविनाशिनीम्॥१९॥

narā muktā bhavanti hi snātvā vā smaraṇādapi|
harau bhaktiṁ ca vindanti sarvaduḥkhavināśinīm||19||

narah — people; muktah — liberated; bhavanti — become; hi — indeed; snatva — by bathing; va — or; smaranat — by remembering; api — even; harau — for Hari; bhaktim — devotion; cha — and; vindanti — obtain; sarva-duhkha-vinashinim — which destroys all sorrow.

19By bathing there, or even by remembering it, people attain liberation — and attain devotion to Hari, which destroys every sorrow8.

Verse 20

नित्यानन्दप्रभुस्तत्र वणिजां तु गृहे गृहे।
करोति कृष्णचैतन्यनामसंकीर्तनं महत्॥२०॥

nityānandaprabhustatra vaṇijāṁ tu gṛhe gṛhe|
karoti kṛṣṇacaitanyanāmasaṁkīrtanaṁ mahat||20||

nityananda-prabhuh — Nityananda Prabhu; tatra — there; vanijam — of the merchants; tu — and; grihe grihe — in house after house; karoti — performs; krishnachaitanya-nama-sankirtanam — the sankirtana of the name of Krishna Chaitanya; mahat — great.

20There Nityananda Prabhu performs, in house after house of the merchants, a great sankirtana of the name of Krishna Chaitanya.

Verse 21

यथा संकीर्तनसुखं नवद्वीपे भवेत् पुरा।
नित्यानन्दप्रसादेन तदेवात्र सुखं परम्॥२१॥

yathā saṁkīrtanasukhaṁ navadvīpe bhavet purā|
nityānandaprasādena tadevātra sukhaṁ param||21||

yatha — as; sankirtana-sukham — the joy of sankirtana; navadvipe — in Navadvipa; bhavet — was; pura — formerly; nityananda-prasadena — by the grace of Nityananda; tat eva — that same; atra — here; sukham — joy; param — supreme.

21The joy of sankirtana that once there was in Navadvipa — that same supreme joy came here too by Nityananda's grace.

Verse 22

उद्धारणगृहे स्थित्वा तेन सार्धं जगद्गुरुः।
गौरचन्द्ररसे मग्नः शान्तिपुरमगात्ततः॥२२॥

uddhāraṇagṛhe sthitvā tena sārdhaṁ jagadguruḥ|
gauracandrarase magnaḥ śāntipuramagāttataḥ||22||

uddharana-grihe — in the house of Uddharana; sthitva — having stayed; tena sardham — together with him; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; gaurachandra-rase — in the rasa of Gaurachandra; magnah — immersed; shantipuram — to Shantipura; agat — went; tatah — then.

22Having stayed in the house of Uddharana9, the Teacher of the world, immersed in the rasa of Gaurachandra, then went with him to Shantipura.

Verse 23

नित्यानन्दमुखं दृष्ट्वा श्रीलाद्वैतो महामतिः।
हुहुङ्कारेण नादेन दिङ्मुखं परिपूरयन्॥२३॥

nityānandamukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā śrīlādvaito mahāmatiḥ|
huhuṅkāreṇa nādena diṅmukhaṁ paripūrayan||23||

nityananda-mukham — the face of Nityananda; drishtva — seeing; shrila-advaitah — Srila Advaita; maha-matih — of great mind; huhunkarena — with the roar "hu-hum"; nadena — with the sound; din-mukham — the quarters; paripurayan — filling.

23Seeing Nityananda's face, the wise Srila Advaita filled all the quarters with a thundering "hu-hum,"

Verse 24

स्तुत्वा परमहर्षेण नमस्कृत्य पुनः पुनः।
तमालिङ्ग्य प्रभुश्चापि प्रणम्य ससुखं वसन्॥२४॥

stutvā paramaharṣeṇa namaskṛtya punaḥ punaḥ|
tamāliṅgya prabhuścāpi praṇamya sasukhaṁ vasan||24||

stutva — having praised; parama-harshena — with the greatest joy; namaskritya — bowing; punah punah — again and again; tam — him; alingya — embracing; prabhuh — the Prabhu (Nityananda); cha api — and; pranamya — bowing; sa-sukham — happily; vasan — staying.

24praised Him with the greatest joy and bowed down again and again. And the Prabhu embraced Him and bowed to Him in turn; having stayed there happily

Verse 25

तस्यापि जनयन् हर्षं नवद्वीपमगात् प्रभुः।
गौराङ्गगुणसंमत्तो जगदाह्लादकारकः॥२५॥

tasyāpi janayan harṣaṁ navadvīpamagāt prabhuḥ|
gaurāṅgaguṇasaṁmatto jagadāhlādakārakaḥ||25||

tasya — to him; api — also; janayan — giving; harsham — joy; navadvipam — to Navadvipa; agat — went; prabhuh — the Prabhu; gauranga-guna-sammattah — intoxicated with Gauranga's qualities; jagat-ahlada-karakah — who gladdens the world.

25and given joy to Him as well, the Prabhu, intoxicated with Gauranga's qualities, He who gladdens the world, went on to Navadvipa.

Thus ends the twenty-second sarga, "The Festival of the Meeting of Sri Nityananda and Advaita" (Shri-nityananda-advaita-sangotsava), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Panihati: a village on the Ganga north of Calcutta; Raghava Pandita, a companion of the Lord, lived there.
  2. That is, the Ganga.
  3. Sri Rama is apparently Ramadasa (Abhirama), Shridama in Krishna's lila; Sundara is Sundarananda; Gauridasa is Gauridasa Pandita. All of them are cowherd friends of Krishna and Balarama in Vraja.
  4. Gadadhara Dasa, a companion of Nityananda, whose heart was filled with the mood of the gopis (not to be confused with Gadadhara Pandita).
  5. Saptagrama: an old trading town in Bengal, near the place where the Ganga, the Yamuna and the Sarasvati part (the Triveni).
  6. Apparently Purandara Pandita, one of Nityananda's companions.
  7. Mukta-veni ("the loosened braid"): the place in Bengal where the three rivers part, as distinct from the Yukta-veni ("the bound braid"), their confluence at Prayaga.
  8. Liberation is only a by-product of the holy place; its highest gift is devotion to Hari, for whose sake Nityananda came there with the sankirtana.
  9. Uddharana Datta: a companion of Nityananda from Saptagrama, of the merchant community.
